prompt: Which statements about the Default user and Redis Cloud role-based access control are true? Select all that apply.
explanation: Every new database is protected by a Default user whose username is default, with a randomly generated Default user password. Once RBAC provides named, least-privilege users, Redis recommends turning the Default user off. Redis Cloud manages database users in the console — ACL SETUSER and several other ACL subcommands are not supported — while MULTI, EXEC, and DISCARD are always permitted (the commands inside a transaction are still checked against RBAC permissions). Passwordless authentication is a Pro-only option that requires the public endpoint to be blocked, not a password rotation on the Free plan.

options.text: Every new Redis Cloud database is protected by a Default user whose username is default
After enabling RBAC, Redis recommends turning off the Default user
ACL SETUSER is not supported in Redis Cloud; users, roles, and ACLs are managed in the console
MULTI and EXEC are denied unless a Redis ACL explicitly grants them to the user
Clearing the Default user's password is the supported way to disable password authentication on a Free plan
